read_extent: All three original author pages as extracted text; complete Commission carbon-pricing subsection across physical pages 13–14 and relevant passages on 18–19. No full 20-page Commission read.
reasoning: The primary plan expressly reserves the outcome of the future ETS review and conditions any flexibility. It does not announce the specific three measures requested in the letter.

Nevertheless, the author uses future-intent language and an advocacy paragraph that can compress announced consideration of flexibility into anticipated exceptions. This is an arguable overstatement, not a necessary assertion that the requested exemptions are already enacted or unconditionally promised.

The adjacent request calls on Germany to advocate changes in the EU ETS. A response sent to German ministries does not by itself establish participation in an identified German federal legislative process. Exact domestic-version gate remains open.
The June author date and later August recipient events must remain separate; redelivery is not proof the document was newly authored in the window.
limits: No present exemption, compatibility of requested reforms, feasibility of decarbonisation or source-intent finding. This review supports a non-issue scope/source note, not an admitted allegation.
